desc: Verify Project Manager authentication using valid email address and password
pre: User account with Project Manager role is active and registered in the system.
steps:
1. Open web browser and navigate to the application login URL.
2. In the Email field, enter the registered Project Manager email address.
3. In the Password field, enter the valid account password.
4. Click the "Sign In" button.
5. Verify successful authentication.
expected: System authenticates the user credentials, initiates a valid session, and grants access without authentication errors.

desc: Verify system rejects Project Manager login with invalid password
pre: Active Project Manager email exists; user is on the login page.
steps:
1. Navigate to the login page.
2. Enter registered Project Manager email address.
3. Enter an incorrect/invalid password.
4. Click "Sign In".
expected: System rejects authentication, displays an error message ("Invalid login credentials"), and does not grant access.

desc: Verify authenticated Project Manager is routed to the Project Manager portal
pre: User authenticates with Project Manager credentials.
steps:
1. Complete sign-in with Project Manager credentials.
2. Observe the landing page URL and dashboard interface.
3. Verify role portal layout.
expected: System directs user to "/project-manager" portal displaying the Project Manager navigation sidebar (Dashboard, Projects, Team, Inventory, Reports, Settings).

desc: Verify inactive or deactivated Project Manager account cannot access protected functions
pre: A Project Manager account has been deactivated by an Administrator.
steps:
1. Navigate to the login page.
2. Enter the deactivated Project Manager email and password.
3. Click "Sign In".
4. If session token was cached, attempt to open "/project-manager".
expected: System denies access, displays account inactive notification, and blocks all protected portal pages and server actions.

desc: Verify invited Project Manager must complete activation before accessing functions
pre: Administrator has sent an invitation to a new PM email; invitation is pending.
steps:
1. Attempt to log in directly with the invited email without completing activation.
2. Attempt to navigate directly to "/project-manager" in an unauthenticated browser.
expected: Access is denied; system requires the user to open the invitation email link and complete account activation.

desc: Verify invited Project Manager sets password >= 8 characters with fixed role
pre: Invited PM opens valid invitation setup link in email.
steps:
1. Open the invitation link in browser.
2. Verify the invited email and assigned role "Project Manager" are displayed read-only.
3. Attempt to enter a password shorter than 8 characters and submit.
4. Enter matching passwords of at least 8 characters and submit.
expected: Short password (<8 chars) is rejected with validation message; entering valid password >= 8 chars completes activation without permitting role changes.

desc: Verify Project Manager can request password-reset link using email address
pre: Project Manager is on the login page and has forgotten password.
steps:
1. On the login screen, click "Forgot Password?".
2. Enter the registered Project Manager email address in the input field.
3. Click "Send reset link".
4. Check recipient email inbox.
expected: System accepts the request and dispatches a secure password-reset link to the registered email address.

desc: Verify password-reset response is generic and does not disclose account registration status
pre: User is on the Forgot Password page.
steps:
1. Enter an unregistered email address (e.g. nonexistent@test.com).
2. Click "Send reset link".
3. Observe displayed confirmation message.
4. Repeat with a registered PM email and compare confirmation message.
expected: System displays identical generic confirmation response ("If an account exists for this email, a reset link has been sent") for both registered and unregistered addresses.

desc: Verify Project Manager can change password in Settings with current password verification
pre: Project Manager is logged in and navigates to Settings > Change Password.
steps:
1. Open Settings > Change Password.
2. Enter current password correctly.
3. Enter new password (at least 8 chars) and matching confirmation.
4. Click "Update Password".
5. Sign out and sign in using the new password.
expected: Password updates successfully; user can log in with new password; old password is no longer accepted.

desc: Verify password change is rejected when new password matches current password
pre: Project Manager is logged in and opens Change Password form in Settings.
steps:
1. Open Settings > Change Password.
2. Enter correct current password.
3. In "New Password" and "Confirm Password", enter the exact same current password.
4. Click "Update Password".
expected: System rejects password change and displays error message indicating new password cannot be the same as current password.

desc: Verify Project Manager can sign out of account securely
pre: Project Manager is logged in.
steps:
1. Click user profile avatar or navigation menu.
2. Click "Sign Out".
3. Observe redirect to login page.
4. Click browser "Back" button.
expected: User session is revoked, browser redirects to login page, and browser back button does not reveal protected project information.

desc: Verify Project Manager profile details (name, email, role) displayed in Settings
pre: Project Manager is authenticated.
steps:
1. Click "Settings" in the navigation sidebar.
2. Inspect the Account Details / Profile section.
expected: Settings displays the Project Manager's full name, registered email address, and assigned role badge ("Project Manager").

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot manage Super Administrator or Administrator accounts
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect the navigation sidebar for account management links.
2. Attempt to navigate directly to "/admin/accounts".
3. Attempt to invoke the user listing API endpoint.
expected: Accounts menu is not visible; direct route navigation returns 403 Forbidden or redirects to PM dashboard; API rejects unauthorized access.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot manage other Project Manager or Foreman accounts
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. In Settings or Team view, check for account creation, role editing, or password reset controls for peers.
2. Attempt to access administrative user management endpoints.
expected: Account management actions are restricted strictly to administrative roles; PM cannot edit peer accounts.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot invite new users or assign system roles
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect Team module and Settings for an "Invite User" button.
2. Attempt to submit an invitation payload with name, email, and role via server action.
expected: User invitation controls are hidden; server-side authorization blocks invitation submissions from PM users.

desc: Verify system rejects user invitations with duplicate emails (Administrative rule validation)
pre: User account with registered email already exists.
steps:
1. Test system invitation endpoint with an already registered email address.
2. Verify system validation behavior.
expected: System validates email uniqueness and rejects invitations for existing registered email addresses.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot resend account invitations to pending users
pre: A pending user invitation exists in the system; PM is logged in.
steps:
1. Inspect accessible UI for pending invitation resend controls.
2. Attempt to invoke invitation resend API endpoint.
expected: Resend invitation action is restricted to authorized account managers; PM cannot trigger invitation emails.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot modify account details of other system users
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Navigate to Team member profiles.
2. Attempt to modify user email, account status, or authentication settings.
3. Send account update mutation directly.
expected: Account-level fields are read-only; mutation is rejected with 403 Forbidden.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot activate or deactivate user accounts individually or in bulk
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect user tables for active/inactive toggle switches or bulk deactivation actions.
2. Attempt to send account status mutation.
expected: Account activation and deactivation controls are completely hidden; server rejects status modification attempts.

desc: Verify self-deactivation prevention rule in account management
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Navigate to Settings -> Profile.
2. Verify there is no option or button to deactivate or delete the current user account.
expected: Account deactivation controls are absent; system prevents self-deactivation through standard user management.

desc: Verify project handover requirement when a Project Manager assigned to an unfinished project is deactivated
pre: Project Manager is assigned to an active unfinished project.
steps:
1. In test environment, Administrator attempts to deactivate the assigned PM.
2. Verify system prompts for a replacement PM.
3. Attempt to bypass handover selection.
expected: System blocks deactivation until a suitable, active Project Manager is designated to inherit the unfinished project.

desc: Verify handover replacement validation enforces role, active status, and assignment limits
pre: Handover selection modal is displayed during PM deactivation.
steps:
1. Attempt to select an inactive user or a Foreman as replacement PM.
2. Attempt to select a PM who exceeds unfinished project limits.
3. Select an active, eligible Project Manager.
expected: System rejects invalid or over-allocated users and only allows confirming handover to an active, qualified Project Manager.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot change user roles or elevate privileges
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect Settings and Team modules for role dropdowns.
2. Attempt to send an API request changing current PM role to Administrator.
expected: Role modification controls are not available; server rejects role change requests from non-admin accounts.

desc: Verify system blocks role changes that conflict with active unfinished project assignments
pre: Project Manager is actively assigned to an ongoing construction project.
steps:
1. In test administrative portal, attempt to change the PM's role to Foreman without reassigning the project.
2. Observe system validation.
expected: System rejects role change and requires active project assignments to be handed over before role modification can proceed.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot send password-reset emails, set temporary passwords, or revoke sessions of other users
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect user profile views for "Send Password Reset" or "Revoke Sessions" buttons.
2. Attempt to call administrative credential management actions.
expected: Administrative password management tools are hidden; server actions block unauthorized credential operations.

desc: Verify permanent account deletion is restricted exclusively to Super Administrator
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect all portal screens for account deletion options.
2. Attempt to call permanent user deletion API route.
expected: Account deletion is completely unavailable to PM; permanent deletion is strictly restricted to Super Administrator.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot view account management activity audit logs
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager.
steps:
1. Inspect Dashboard activity feed and Settings for system-wide account audit logs.
2. Attempt to query administrative audit log endpoints.
expected: PM dashboard displays only project-related activity; system-wide account creation/modification logs remain restricted to administrators.

desc: Verify Project Manager access is restricted exclusively to assigned projects
pre: PM is assigned to Project A; Project B is assigned to a different Project Manager.
steps:
1. Log in as Project Manager.
2. Navigate to Projects page.
3. Verify Project A appears in the list.
4. Verify Project B does NOT appear in the list.
5. Attempt to navigate directly to Project B URL (/project-manager/projects/[Project-B-ID]).
expected: Project B is not listed in project directory, and direct URL access returns 404/Access Denied without disclosing Project B records.

desc: Verify Accounts management module is restricted from Project Manager access
pre: Project Manager is logged in.
steps:
1. Inspect the navigation sidebar for an Accounts link.
2. Attempt to navigate directly to "/admin/accounts" or "/admin" in the browser address bar.
expected: Accounts module is absent from PM sidebar; entering admin URLs redirects to PM portal or displays 403 Forbidden.

desc: Verify Project Manager has authorized access to Team module
pre: Project Manager is logged in.
steps:
1. Click "Team" in navigation sidebar.
2. Verify Team page loads with member categories and work groups.
expected: Team module opens successfully showing company personnel roster and work group management controls.

desc: Verify Project Manager portal provides access to Dashboard, Projects, Inventory, Reports, and Settings
pre: Project Manager is logged in.
steps:
1. Click each navigation item in sidebar: Dashboard, Projects, Team, Inventory, Reports, and Settings.
2. Verify each destination loads with role-appropriate permissions.
expected: All core PM navigation items load smoothly with proper Project Manager views (and read-only inventory browsing).

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify Dashboard displays accessible projects with current status and progress
pre: PM has assigned projects with varied progress levels.
steps:
1. Navigate to Dashboard.
2. Review "Projects" section.
3. Verify project name, location, status badge (Ongoing/Completed), and calculated progress %.
expected: Only assigned projects are displayed with accurate calculated progress bars and current status badges.

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify Dashboard metric summary counts scoped to accessible projects
pre: Assigned projects have known ongoing/completed counts and pending requests.
steps:
1. Inspect top metric cards on PM Dashboard.
2. Compare Ongoing Projects, Completed Projects, Pending Material Requests, and Pending Equipment Requests counts against accessible project data.
expected: Metric summary cards accurately reflect counts belonging strictly to PM's assigned projects.

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify active project planned progress, actual progress, budget, expense, and remaining budget summary
pre: Assigned project has budget and saved cost/progress data.
steps:
1. On Dashboard, locate the active project financial & progress overview card.
2. Compare Planned Progress, Actual Progress, Allocated Budget, Recorded Expenditure, and Remaining Budget.
expected: Values match calculated project metrics; Remaining Budget equals Allocated Budget minus Recorded Actual Expense.

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify Dashboard displays pending material and equipment requests with details
pre: Pending material and equipment requests exist in assigned project.
steps:
1. Navigate to Dashboard > Pending Requests widget.

expected: Pending requests display Request Number, Project Name, Requester Name, Request Date, and Priority badge (Low/Medium/High/Urgent).

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify recent project activity feed navigates to associated project or record
pre: Recent progress saves, requests, or document uploads exist.
steps:
1. On Dashboard, locate "Recent Activity" feed.
2. Click an activity entry (e.g. progress update or request).
3. Observe target screen.
expected: Activity item opens the corresponding project view or record details without navigation errors.

category: 3.1.3. View the Dashboard and Project Portfolio
desc: Verify team availability and equipment availability summaries on Dashboard
pre: Team members and equipment records exist in system.
steps:
1. Inspect Dashboard availability widgets for Team and Equipment.
2. Verify available vs assigned counts.
expected: Availability figures reflect real-time allocations without exposing unassigned project data.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot create new projects (creation restricted to administrative roles)
pre: Project Manager is logged in and viewing Projects directory.
steps:
1. Navigate to Projects page.
2. Inspect the page for a "Create Project" or "New Project" button.
3. Attempt to access project creation URL (/projects/new) or send creation mutation.
expected: Project creation button is absent; direct creation route redirects or displays 403 Forbidden.

desc: Verify project creation validation mandates project name, Project Manager, and Foreman
pre: Project creation form accessed in administrative test session.
steps:
1. Open Project Creation dialog.
2. Attempt to save without entering project name.
3. Attempt to save without selecting a PM or Foreman.
4. Enter all mandatory fields and save.
expected: System validates required fields, highlights missing inputs, and only creates project when name, PM, and Foreman are provided.

desc: Verify system rejects project management assignments that violate unfinished-project restrictions
pre: Project Manager has reached maximum unfinished project allocation limit.
steps:
1. In administrative portal, attempt to assign this PM to a new ongoing project.
2. Observe validation feedback.
expected: System rejects assignment, displaying an alert that the selected Project Manager has exceeded active project capacity.

desc: Verify Project Manager views project working days, planned dates, and actual completion date configured by administration
pre: Project Manager is assigned to active project.
steps:
1. Open assigned Project Details page.
2. Review Project Overview and Schedule settings.
3. Verify display of working days (e.g., Mon-Sat) and completion date targets.
expected: Project information, working days, and target/actual completion dates display accurately as configured by administration.

desc: Verify Project Manager cannot delete projects (project deletion restricted to administrative roles)
pre: Project Manager is viewing assigned project details.
steps:
1. Inspect project overview and settings menus for a "Delete Project" option.
2. Attempt to invoke project deletion server action.
expected: Delete project option is absent from PM interface; server action rejects unauthorized deletion attempts.

desc: Verify distinction between allocated project budget and planned cost estimate
pre: Assigned project has Allocated Budget (e.g. ₱5,000,000) and Cost Estimate total (e.g. ₱4,200,000).
steps:
1. Open assigned project > Overview tab.
2. Inspect budget and cost cards.
3. Open Cost Estimate tab.
expected: Allocated budget is clearly labeled as "Budget" and distinguished from the planned cost baseline ("Planned") calculated in cost estimate.

desc: Verify project Ongoing and Completed status derived from calculated progress
pre: Assigned project progress reaches 100%.
steps:
1. View project status badge in project header and directory.
2. Verify status updates from Ongoing to Completed when progress reaches 100%.
expected: Project status badge reflects calculated progress status accurately.

desc: Verify completed projects remain accessible for viewing and review
pre: At least one assigned project is marked Completed.
steps:
1. In Projects directory, filter by "Completed" status.
2. Click on the completed project.
3. Browse Overview, Progress, Gantt, Materials, Equipment, Expenses, and Reports.
expected: Completed project opens in full read-only review mode with all historical records, progress entries, and reports intact.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify Team member directory organization into four categories
pre: Team members exist in database across categories.
steps:
1. Navigate to Team module.
2. Click through tabs: Management, Skilled Workers, Engineers & Architects, and Subcontractors.
3. Verify members listed in each tab.
expected: Personnel are correctly segmented into their respective professional categories.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify Project Manager has read-only access to Team member master records and cannot edit personnel details
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager in Team module.
steps:

2. Click on a worker or engineer record.
3. Verify absence of "Edit Member" or "New Member" buttons.
4. Verify member details (trade, category, hire date) are displayed read-only.
expected: Member details are display-only; creating and editing master personnel records is restricted to administrative roles.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify subcontractor records display required company name in Team module
pre: Subcontractor personnel exist in system.
steps:
1. Navigate to Team -> Subcontractors tab.
2. Inspect listed subcontractor personnel.
3. Open subcontractor detail dialog.
expected: System displays subcontractor member details along with their associated company name.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify member weekly schedule displays nonnegative default hourly rates and 0-24 hour limits
pre: User is viewing member profile in Team module.
steps:
1. Open member details modal.
2. Inspect hourly rate value (verify nonnegative).
3. Inspect daily working hours across Monday to Sunday (verify within 0 to 24 hours).
expected: System displays nonnegative hourly rates and daily working schedule values strictly within the 0 to 24 hour range.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify display of member weekly working schedule, hours, availability, and assignments
pre: Skilled worker has recorded weekly schedule (e.g. 8h Mon-Sat, 0 Sun) and default rate.
steps:
1. Open a skilled worker profile in Team module.
2. Inspect Weekly Schedule grid, Total Weekly Hours, Hourly Rate, and Work Groups.
expected: Schedule displays 7-day breakdown, total hours, default rate (₱/hr), availability badge, and current project/crew assignments.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify Project Manager cannot delete member records from the Team module
pre: User is logged in as Project Manager in Team module.
steps:
1. Select a member in the Team roster.
2. Check context menu and action bar for a "Delete Member" option.
3. Attempt to invoke member deletion action directly.
expected: Delete member action is hidden from PM; server rejects unauthorized member deletion requests.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify search and filter functionality on Team member directory
pre: Multiple members exist in Team directory.
steps:
1. In Team search bar, enter a member's name or trade.
2. Filter by availability (Available / Assigned).
3. Clear search and filter.
expected: Member list dynamically filters matching the search query and returns to full list upon clearing.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify Project Manager can create, edit, and delete work groups (crews)
pre: Project Manager is on Team page > Groups section.
steps:

2. Enter Group Name (e.g. "Masonry Team A") and select members.
3. Click Save.
4. Edit group name to "Masonry Team A - Revised" and add a member.
5. Delete the disposable test group.
expected: Group is created successfully, updates persist, and deletion removes the group without deleting individual member profiles.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify group name uniqueness validation is case-insensitive
pre: A group named "Concrete Crew" already exists.
steps:

3. Attempt to save.
expected: System rejects duplicate name and displays validation error ("A group with this name already exists").

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify work group can contain multiple members and member can belong to multiple groups

steps:

2. Create Group 2 with Worker A and Worker D.

expected: Both groups save with multiple members, and Worker A's profile correctly shows membership in both Group 1 and Group 2.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify Project Manager can assign members or crew groups to project tasks or standalone phases
pre: Assigned project has tasks in schedule/Gantt view.

expected: Assigned workforce is saved to the task and appears under Task Workforce.

category: 3.1.5. Manage Team Members and Work Groups
desc: Verify member assignment details derive from recorded project schedule assignments

steps:

3. Edit category name to "Substructure & Foundation".
4. Create a temporary empty category and delete it.

category: 3.1.6. Prepare the Cost Estimate and Work Breakdown
desc: Verify Project Manager can create and maintain tasks and subtasks in work breakdown
pre: Phase exists in Cost Estimate.
steps:

3. Add a child subtask under the task.
4. Verify hierarchy and roll-up totals.
expected: Task and subtask are created in correct WBS hierarchy; subtask costs aggregate to parent task without double-counting.

category: 3.1.6. Prepare the Cost Estimate and Work Breakdown
desc: Verify standalone phase with no child tasks is supported as an independently planned work item
pre: A phase with no child tasks is created.
steps:

2. Enter estimated quantity, unit, planned dates, and cost components directly on the phase.
3. Save and inspect progress tracking.
expected: Standalone phase functions as an independent work item with its own progress tracking, cost baseline, and schedule bar.

category: 3.1.6. Prepare the Cost Estimate and Work Breakdown
desc: Verify maintaining work-item planning parameters (dates, quantity, unit, priority, milestone, predecessor)

desc: Verify maintaining planned material assignments with quantities, units, and unit costs

category: 3.1.6. Prepare the Cost Estimate and Work Breakdown
desc: Verify maintaining planned equipment and other cost itemized breakdowns

category: 3.1.6. Prepare the Cost Estimate and Work Breakdown
desc: Verify setting default labor cost percentage (0-100%) and labor adjustments

desc: Verify display of planned durations, dependencies, and calculated progress on Gantt chart
pre: Project has scheduled tasks with progress logged.

pre: Notifications exist for multiple users in the system.
steps:
1. As Project Manager, view notification bell list.
2. Attempt to mark as read or delete a notification belonging to another user via API.
3. Observe response.
expected: System permits mutation only on notifications where recipient_id equals the current user; other users' notifications cannot be altered.

desc: Verify project drawings, documents, and incident evidence are securely stored in configured storage buckets
pre: Project Manager uploads a drawing PDF and an incident photo attachment.
steps:

2. Upload incident evidence photo in Safety Incidents.
3. Verify generated storage URLs and bucket destinations.
expected: Drawings are stored in project documents bucket; incident photos stored in incident evidence bucket with proper access policies.

desc: Verify upload controls validate file extensions and reject unsupported MIME types and oversized files
pre: Project Manager is on document or attachment upload dialog.
steps:
1. Attempt to upload an executable file (.exe, .bat).
2. Attempt to upload a document exceeding 25MB.
3. Upload a valid PDF / PNG under 25MB.
expected: Executable file is rejected with unsupported format error; oversized file is rejected with file size limit error; valid file uploads successfully.

category: 3.2.3. Data Integrity and Business Rule Consistency
desc: Verify form controls enforce numeric validation rules rejecting negative values and invalid hours
pre: Project Manager opens task edit or progress log entry modal.
steps:

2. Enter 25 in Daily Working Hours field.
3. Attempt to save the form.
expected: Form displays inline validation error messages; inputs reject invalid values and prevent submission.

category: 3.2.3. Data Integrity and Business Rule Consistency
desc: Verify saved progress log entry is strictly associated with one target work breakdown item
pre: Project Manager opens daily progress logging modal.
steps:

2. Log completed quantity and submit.
3. Inspect database / API payload for progress record.
expected: Progress log record contains exactly one valid task_id or phase_id; progress cannot be ambiguously linked to multiple items.

category: 3.2.3. Data Integrity and Business Rule Consistency
desc: Verify saved progress log attendance snapshots remain fixed when worker hourly rates change
pre:

steps:

category: 3.2.3. Data Integrity and Business Rule Consistency
desc: Verify expense and equipment ledgers accurately aggregate distinct transactions without duplication
pre: Project has saved progress logs with equipment and unplanned costs, and multiple revisions.
steps:

2. Compare ledger total with sum of active saved log entries.
3. Verify historical superseded revisions do not duplicate ledger rows.
expected: Ledger displays current saved entries accurately; no double counting or ghost entries appear in totals.

category: 3.2.3. Data Integrity and Business Rule Consistency
desc: Verify optimistic concurrency detects stale updates when two users edit the same task concurrently
pre: Task edit modal is open simultaneously by two users.
steps:
1. User A saves changes to task duration and scope.
2. User B, on unrefreshed modal, attempts to save modifications.
3. Observe system feedback.
expected: System detects version mismatch, prevents overwriting User A's changes, and displays a warning to reload latest data.

desc: Verify system displays clear error notifications when network disconnects or action fails
pre: Project Manager is on an edit form.
steps:

expected: System displays a user-friendly error banner or toast notification explaining the failure, without crashing or blanking the page.

desc: Verify mandatory fields display required markers and clear inline validation messages
pre: Project Manager opens "Add Task" or "Submit Material Request" modal.
steps:

2. Click Submit / Save.
3. Observe input field styling and validation feedback.
expected: Required fields display red borders and descriptive validation text below each field; form focus moves to first invalid field.

desc: Verify record viewing and editing workflows use dedicated dialogs without disrupting background state
pre: User is on Project Gantt chart or Inventory table.
steps:
1. Click on a record to open read-only progress modal.
2. Click edit button to transition to edit modal.
3. Close modal without saving.
expected: Modals open smoothly over the current view; closing modal preserves underlying table scroll position and active filter state.

desc: Verify all monetary values throughout the portal display Philippine Peso (₱) symbol and thousand separators
pre: Project has recorded budgets, estimate costs, and expenses (e.g. 1500000).
steps:

2. Verify formatting of numeric currency values.
expected: All monetary amounts display with "₱" symbol and standard thousands separators (e.g. "₱1,500,000.00"), with zero amounts formatted as "₱0.00".

desc: Verify detail views present full source context including project, task, record date, and creator
pre: Saved progress log, incident report, or request exists.
steps:

2. Verify header displays project name, task title, submission timestamp, and creator name/role.
expected: Full source context is clearly displayed in the header banner, establishing verifiable provenance for every record.

desc: Verify responsive layout and horizontal scrolling behavior on large tables and Gantt charts
pre: User opens Gantt chart or extensive inventory table on 1366x768 and 1920x1080 display viewports.

2. Verify table headers remain aligned with data columns.
3. Test horizontal scroll on Gantt timeline and ledger tables.
expected: Tables provide smooth horizontal scrolling without layout breaking, column truncation, or clipped action buttons.

desc: Verify historical progress logs, document reviews, and account actions maintain permanent audit records

steps:

3. Verify previous history entries cannot be overwritten or wiped.
expected: Complete append-only audit trail is maintained and visible, preserving historical accountability.
